title: Reptiles and amphibians
examples: What is the main difference between a snake and a salamander?
Do reptiles and amphibians need water to live?
How do their eggs differ from ours?

explain.say: Today we learn about reptiles and amphibians. These groups of animals are very different.
Reptiles usually have dry, protective scales on their skin. Amphibians often have moist, smooth skin.
Both groups of animals are cold-blooded. This means their body temperature changes with the environment.
Many reptiles and amphibians lay eggs. These eggs are often laid in specific environments.
A concrete example is the lizard. Lizards have dry scales and lay leathery eggs on land.
For a real-life example, think about a garden pond. Frogs live there, using the water and land.

faq.a: Most reptiles do have scales for protection. Some exceptions exist, but scales are common.
asks: What is on a snake's skin?

faq.q: Do amphibians always live in water?
faq.a: No, many amphibians can live both on land and in water. They need moist environments.
asks: Can frogs live on dry ground?
Where do amphibians spend their time?

faq.q: What does 'cold-blooded' mean for these animals?
faq.a: It means their body temperature matches the temperature around them. They need the environment to keep warm.
asks: Do they need the sun to warm up?
How do they control their body heat?

faq.a: No, some reptile eggs are very leathery. The shell material can vary greatly.
asks: What kind of shell do crocodiles lay?
Are all reptile eggs the same?

faq.q: How does a frog change its skin?
faq.a: When a tadpole becomes a frog, its skin changes to become more suitable for land life.
asks: Does a frog's skin get dry?
What happens to a tadpole's skin?

facts: Reptiles typically have dry, scaly skin.
Both groups are ectothermic, meaning they are cold-blooded.
Eggs can be laid on land or near water.

quiz.say: A snake has dry scales, while a frog has moist skin. Which group is the snake in?
quiz.why: Snakes are reptiles and are known for their dry, scaly skin.

wrong.1: Amphibians usually have smooth, moist skin, not dry scales.
wrong.2: Mammals have fur or hair, which is different from scales.
wrong.3: Fish usually have scales, but the skin texture is different from dry reptile scales.

quiz.say: A lizard basking in the sun is showing it is:
quiz.why: Lizards need external heat from the sun to raise their body temperature.

wrong.0: Warm-blooded animals generate their own body heat, like mammals.
wrong.1: While they need water sometimes, 'cold-blooded' describes their temperature regulation.
wrong.2: This describes nocturnal habits, not their body temperature regulation.

quiz.say: If an animal lays leathery eggs on dry ground, it is most likely a:
quiz.why: Reptiles are known for laying eggs, often leathery ones, on land.

wrong.1: Amphibians usually lay eggs that require water to develop properly.
wrong.2: Birds have hard, calcified shells on their eggs.
wrong.3: Fish eggs are typically laid in large numbers in water.
